turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: No, no, O-lan, do not talk like this. You will live, I will take care of you.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Now, my son, I have asked the maid to make a new silk dress for you to take to your bride. You must take care of her, just as I have taken care of you.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: I will, mistress. I will make the dress the finest I can, with silk from our own house.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: Mother, do not worry, I will take good care of the maid and make her happy. I promise to make you proud and give you grandchildren to love.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I am glad you have promised to take care of her, my son. But tell me, when will you and the maid be married?

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: You must not worry about these things, O-lan. You must rest and get well.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: But, Wang Lung, the wedding must take place soon, before I am no longer here to see it. I want my son to have a good wife and a happy life.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: O-lan, you must not think about such things now, you must think about getting well, for me, for our son, for our family

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: Mother, do not worry, I will marry the maid as soon as possible, and I will make you proud. I will give you many grandchildren to love before the winter is over.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I am glad you promise to marry soon, my son. But Wang Lung, you must help me see that it is done, for I will not be here to oversee it.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: You are talking too much, O-lan, and exhausting yourself. Leave the arrangements to me, I will see that the wedding takes place as soon as possible.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I will start making arrangements for the wedding right away, Father, and I will make sure to ask for your guidance as well.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I am glad you will make arrangements, my son, but I must speak to the maid about her role in the household after she is married

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: I am honored that you would consider me for your son's bride, Mother, but I am not sure if I am worthy, and I do not want to bring shame to your family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will not hear you say you are not worthy, child. You have been a good daughter to us, and Wang Lung will be grateful to have you as his daughter-in-law.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: I am truly grateful for your kindness, Mother, but I am afraid I am not worthy of being the daughter-in-law to a woman as kind and wise as you.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will make sure to teach you all the ways of our household, child, so that you will be able to care for your father-in-law when I am gone

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: But, Mother, I do not know if I am prepared to take on such a great responsibility, especially with your health declining as it is.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Do not worry about my health, child, for I have lived a long life and I will not burden you with my care.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will not be a burden to you, child. You must marry my son and have children of your own, so that our household will not dwindle.
